edges.effect_quant: The clearest large observational estimates cluster around a 3-fold Achilles rupture signal, with one large case-control study reporting OR 4.1 for Achilles rupture and a population cohort reporting a standardized incidence ratio of 3.1 after first exposure.
edges.population: adults prescribed systemic fluoroquinolone antibiotics in population cohorts, insurer databases, and regional case-control analyses
edges.mechanism: Fluoroquinolones appear to impair tendon extracellular matrix turnover and collagen integrity, which matters most in weight-bearing tendons such as the Achilles and can be amplified by corticosteroids, older age, or mechanical load.
edges.summary: This is one of the more established fluoroquinolone safety signals. The evidence is observational rather than randomized, but across several large datasets the Achilles tendon repeatedly emerges as the site where rupture risk increases most clearly after exposure.
edges.caveats: Absolute risk remains low, so most exposed patients will not rupture a tendon. The signal is strongest for Achilles rupture, older adults, and concomitant corticosteroid use, so this edge should be interpreted as a selective but clinically real class harm rather than a universal consequence of every short course.

evidence.citation: van der Linden P 2007 Eur J Clin Pharmacol
evidence.notes: Use of fluroquinolone and risk of Achilles tendon rupture: a population-based cohort study.
